questions.q: How does kind run a Kubernetes cluster?
o: Each node is a Docker container running systemd, containerd and Kubernetes
Each node is a virtual machine started by a hypervisor
The control plane runs as a process on your host without any container
Nodes are Pods scheduled on a remote cloud cluster
questions.w: kind stands for Kubernetes IN Docker: node containers bootstrapped with kubeadm. It needs only Docker.

questions.q: A Pod using an image you just built locally ends in ErrImagePull on kind. What is the most likely fix?
o: Run kind load docker-image so the nodes have the image
Restart the Docker daemon on the host
Change the Service type to LoadBalancer
Delete the namespace and create it again
questions.w: The nodes have their own container runtime and cannot see host images. Load the image (or use a local registry) and use a fixed tag.

questions.q: Why avoid the latest tag for locally loaded images?
o: Kubernetes then defaults to imagePullPolicy Always and pulls from a registry
The latest tag is not allowed by kind and is rejected at creation time
Docker deletes local images tagged latest after about one hour of idle time
Services cannot select Pods that use the latest tag in their image field
questions.w: With a fixed tag the default policy is IfNotPresent, which uses the loaded image.

questions.q: How can a kind cluster publish ports 80 and 443 to your host?
o: extraPortMappings in the kind config, plus an ingress controller
Running kubectl proxy as a background service
Setting hostNetwork on every Deployment
Nothing is needed, kind publishes all node ports by default
questions.w: kind does not publish node ports by default. Configure extraPortMappings on a node and install ingress-nginx, or use kubectl port-forward.

questions.q: Why does a LoadBalancer Service stay Pending on kind?
o: There is no cloud controller to create a load balancer
kind blocks the LoadBalancer type in its admission rules
The Service has no selector
The node image is too old
questions.w: Install MetalLB or cloud-provider-kind to assign external IPs locally.

questions.q: Which use is kind best suited for?
o: Disposable clusters in CI to test manifests, charts and operators
Running a production banking platform on a single laptop
Measuring the performance of a production workload
Hosting a shared team cluster with high availability and cloud storage
questions.w: kind is fast and disposable but single-host, resource-bound and without cloud features.

questions.q: What is the main difference between kind and minikube?
o: kind runs nodes as containers for tests and CI; minikube uses drivers and addons
kind runs only on Linux hosts while minikube runs only on macOS laptops
kind is meant for production clusters while minikube is only for learning
kind uses its own Kubernetes fork that has different APIs from upstream
questions.w: Both run real Kubernetes. minikube adds addons, dashboard and tunnel; kind is lighter and easier for multi-node and CI.

questions.q: Why pin the kindest/node image version?
o: It fixes the Kubernetes version, so tests match what production runs
It determines how many nodes the cluster can have
It selects the CNI plugin used for pod networking
It sets the Docker version used on the host
questions.w: Testing on a different minor version can hide removed APIs or changed defaults.
